attempt: port CAMB's SECOND-ORDER tight-coupling EXIT values into perturbations.evolve
motivation: equations.f90:352-370 shows CAMB uses the second-order branch because second_order_tightcoupling is a compile-time .true. It sets the photon octupole y(g_ix+3) and polarization l=2,3 from pig and pigdot, whereas our code installed only the first-order values and never touched fg(3) at all. Since this acts on the acoustic amplitude exactly where the BAO peak sits, it was a plausible source of the +2.5% peak error.
what_was_added: pigdot_tc in the tight-coupling branch (equations.f90:2512-2516), captured for the exit

measured_result.grid: 12 k points from 0.02 to 3.0 h/Mpc, z=0, reference CAMB with 4096 points

verdict: THE PATCH IS HARMFUL AND WAS DROPPED (git stash drop).
how_this_was_established: the median is bit-identical between the two runs (1.00742 both), and every k from 0.17 upward is bit-identical too. Only k=0.02..0.13 moved, and k=0.05 collapsed to 0.00533. A change that alters nothing except to destroy one low-k point is a numerical defect, not a physics improvement.
likely_cause_not_chased: our pigdot is computed from qg_e and the RSA-substituted qgdot_tc, while CAMB's EV%pigdot comes from a different stage of its own tight-coupling block. The k/opacity weighting also becomes extreme at early times when opacity is huge, and our kap_safe floor may not reproduce CAMB's exact evaluation point. Any of these could produce the collapse; none was verified.

baseline_linear_accuracy_on_this_grid.shape: BAO peak top +2.49%, high-k tail +0.53..0.77%, low k +1.25..1.50%

what_this_leaves.gap: max|dev| is 5x the target, and the worst point is the BAO peak top, which is the same place it has been for many attempts

cumulative_note: this is the second attempt in a row that was motivated by the CAMB source and failed. The first was the constant RSA threshold, which was a genuine bug in the torch port and was kept. This one is different: it was a change to the reference numpy solver, and it broke it. The distinction matters - the torch fixes were correcting a port that had drifted, whereas this was altering the thing everything else is validated against.
